items.title: Junior Mance Part I interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, New York City, New York, July 27, 1995…
items.q: I was playing with Dizzy at the time and Norman Granz was the producer of it.

ctx.x: What was it like working with Joe?

With Joe it was great. I knew Joe from Chicago anyway, Joe lived, I think he grew up in Chicago, he was born in Georgia. And it was a good experience working with Joe. I had my trio working with Joe, which was Bob Cranshaw and Mickey Roker and myself. And we had a good time. We had the same manager, John Levy, and he thought it was a good idea to put the two together, to solve two things. We usually played a short set before Joe came on and then played for Joe. And that was a good experience. I really liked…
Nat told us some great stories about some of his compositions.

items.title: Junior Mance Part II interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 18, 1999 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: I was playing with Dizzy at the time... I guess I was in my third year with Dizzy... Playing with Dizzy those three years, I probably learned more... he’d invite me over and he had a studio in his basement. And we’d go down there and he’d show me like alternate chord changes

ctx.x: Well you’re mentioning Gene Ammons reminds me — I wanted to ask you about — for the first part of your career you were playing with different combos and stuff. And eventually you got to a point where you started becoming your own leader, of your trio. © Fillius Jazz Archive -5-

Yeah. That was years later though after Gene Ammons. I think it was about 1961 that I gave serious thought to becoming a leader. Because I made my first record as a leader in ’58 or ’59, it was a Verve record called “Just Plain Junior.” I was playing with Dizzy at the time. And Norman Granz, who then was the owner of Verve records, was also the producer. So he came out of the booth during the break and said, “How would you like to do your own album?” And I was speechless. I didn’t know what to say. Finally I said…
Yeah. I have that CD you mentioned.
